judgment.reasoning: The agreement discloses the existence of "administration and arrangement charges" and a variable "tariff of charges" but does not state the actual amounts of these charges in the agreement itself, instead requiring the Borrower to request a separate document. More importantly, the agreement contains no fair value assessment or justification at all — there is no analysis of the relationship between the price charged (interest, fees, administration/arrangement charges) and the benefits provided to the consumer. Excerpt [2] establishes that manufacturer firms "must consider all the costs and charges a consumer may incur" when assessing the price charged, and excerpt [4] confirms this extends to "all interest, fees and charges a consumer may incur" for consumer credit products like personal loans. Excerpt [5] further requires that "firms must still be able to demonstrate that the benefits were reasonable relative to the price" and that firms must consider how charging structures are designed. The document's explicit statement that fair value justification is "Not addressed in this document" is a direct gap against this requirement — the retrieved excerpts show that firms must actively assess and be able to demonstrate fair value, not merely disclose that fees exist and may vary. The ability to vary the tariff "from time to time" with only "reasonable notice" (clause 6.3), absent any fair value framework governing how such charges are set or reviewed, compounds the concern, as there is no indication the administration/arrangement charges or their variation have been assessed for fair value as required.
